subject: Rate uplift concession and usage smoothing proposal
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@mayatech.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected overrun during integration test — request for temporary uplift

Hi Jonas,

Quick note from our side — during yesterday's integration run we pushed a large batch of fine-tuning / scoring calls and blew past our monthly quota window. We're seeing sustained throttles that are killing the downstream job orchestration for a limited set of endpoints. I'm attaching a small usage export and a snippet of the server logs.

Can Redwood provide a short-term rate lift or a temporary burst allowance while we patch our client-side batching? We need a safety net for the next 48–72 hours to complete the rollout without data loss. We'll accept a retroactive reconciliation and are open to a blended uplift/credit to keep billing predictable.

We'd ideally like to:
- Get a temporary uplift to avoid 429s for ~72 hours
- Have a clear true-up approach after the window (no surprise invoices)
- Confirm PO and procurement timeline so billing lines up

Attaching: mayatech-usage-report-20260828.csv, logfile-snippet.txt

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of ML Engineering
MayaTech
maya@mayatech.com

From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@mayatech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected overrun during integration test — request for temporary uplift

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the quick context and the attachments — the export was helpful. Short answer: yes, we can support a short-term uplift while you finalize client batching. A few thoughts/options so we can move quickly:

Option A — Emergency uplift (fastest):
- Temporary rate multiplier at 2x base rate for a 72-hour window starting when you confirm.
- Retroactive true-up billed at the uplifted rate, with a credit cap equal to the uplifted usage beyond your committed window (this is the simplest commercially).

Option B — Blended uplift + escrow (preferred to avoid surprise spend):
- Grant a temporary throughput floor for 72 hours and place a portion of the uplifted fees into an "escrow" that is reconciled post-window. If the burst usage was genuinely required (per usage evidence) we apply the escrow toward the final invoice; otherwise we credit it back.
- Requires a short escalation sheet and a signed acknowledgement of scope (small paperwork).

We can do either; Ben and Laura are copied for billing and PO handling. If you want the blended escrow path we'll share a short one-page addendum and DocuSign link — we can turn it around within a day once procurement confirms.

Two asks from our side:
1) Confirmation of the exact endpoints and times you expect to run the burst so we can scope routing and capacity (helps avoid cross-customer impact).
2) Estimated total additional tokens or calls (ballpark fine) so we can size the escrow.

I'll flag this as RDW-8421 on our side. If you confirm, we'll provision the temporary uplift and share the addendum + DocuSign.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

Maya — quick note from finance:

We can support the blended-escrow approach. Practical specifics we need to finalize before provisioning:
- PO or written procurement confirmation (email is ok for emergency provisioning, PO required for invoicing later)
- Escrow amount = suggested uplifted estimate * 0.6 by default (we can adjust with supporting evidence)
- Invoicing cadence: we will issue a provisional invoice for the uplifted window, and the final true-up will appear on the next monthly statement with a reconciliation line.

If procurement can email acceptance to procurement@redwood.com we can start provisioning today (we'll also need the HubSpot deal id — jonas has that).
